rules.title: Security deposit cap (1.5x monthly rent)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit above one and one-half times one month's rent. Prepaid rent held to secure future rent, including last month's rent, counts toward the cap, and any annual increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent; annual increase capped at 10% of current deposit

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt if owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling, unless the tenant sends a written request and 30 days pass.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (tenant may opt in by written request, effective 30 days later).
rules.quoted_span:
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional 
yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

rules.title: Security deposit return within 30 days of tenancy termination
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the security deposit plus interest, less permitted deductions, with an itemized list of deductions sent by registered or certified mail. A tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld.
rules.key_value: 30 days; double damages for wrongful withholding

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt if owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling, unless the tenant requests coverage in writing.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Where a tenant breaks the lease, the 30 days run from re-rental or lease expiry, whichever is first.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (opt-in by tenant request).
rules.quoted_span:
Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security 
deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant

rules.title: Security deposit must be held in interest-bearing account
rules.requirement: Landlords holding security deposits for ten or fewer units must place them in an insured New Jersey bank or savings and loan in an interest-bearing account. Interest belongs to the tenant, and the landlord must give the tenant written notice of the account details within 30 days and at each annual interest payment.
rules.key_value: Interest-bearing account; notice within 30 days of receipt

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential rentals; seasonal rentals of up to 125 consecutive days are excluded from this section; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant opts in.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt if owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling, unless the tenant requests coverage.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Seasonal use or rental (not more than 125 consecutive days by a person with a permanent residence elsewhere) is excluded.

rules.exemptions: Seasonal rentals; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (opt-in).
rules.quoted_span:
deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an 
interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit.

rules.title: Security deposit return within 5 business days after displacement
rules.requirement: When a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit within five business days. The landlord must tell the tenant within three business days where to collect it.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies when a public official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified that displacement is expected to last longer than seven days.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Tenant displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation, with an official notice or certification of displacement longer than 7 days.

rules.quoted_span:
Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or 
evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit.

rules.title: Good cause required for lease non-renewal (Anti-Eviction Act)
rules.requirement: Residential landlords may not refuse to renew a written or oral lease unless they have good cause, as enumerated in the eviction section of the Act.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental properties, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excluded (separate rules apply).
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Motels, hotels, and transient or seasonal units are excluded.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient or seasonal units.
rules.quoted_span:
may fail to renew any lease, 
regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.

rules.title: Source of lawful income protection (Law Against Discrimination)
rules.requirement: The Law Against Discrimination requires equal treatment in renting housing regardless of listed characteristics, including source of lawful income.

coverage_conditions.summary: All landlord-tenant relationships except two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and certain single-sex or age-restricted residences (as to familial status).
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Excludes two-family owner-occupied dwellings and rooms in owner- or resident-occupied single homes.

rules.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for one sex or age-restricted housing (as to familial status).
rules.quoted_span:
mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.

rules.title: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control (30 years)
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any municipal rent control ordinance for 30 years after construction is completed. New Jersey has no statewide rent cap; municipalities may adopt rent control or leveling by ordinance.

coverage_conditions.summary: Exemption applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings for 30 years after completion of construction; they are outside local rent control during that period.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Multiple dwellings only. Units with government-subsidized rents may also be exempt from local rent control.

rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings for 30 years after completion; rents subsidized by governmental funding may also be exempt.
rules.interaction: Limits the reach of local rent control ordinances. The state has no laws that establish, govern or control rents, and municipalities may pass rent control or rent leveling ordinances.
rules.quoted_span:
newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

rules.title: Rent increases must not be unconscionable and must follow notice rules
rules.requirement: A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal rent increase ordinance. Before evicting for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.
rules.key_value: No unconscionable increase; written notice of increase required

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act; local rent control ordinances may impose stricter limits.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Unconscionability is fact-specific (amount of increase, landlord expenses and profitability, comparable rents, bargaining position).

rules.interaction: Increase must also comply with municipal rent control ordinances. Tenants may complain to a local rent control board where one exists; otherwise a judge decides unconscionability in the nonpayment eviction action.
rules.quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: No mid-lease rent increases
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot raise the rent during the lease term. The old lease must be terminated by proper written notice and a new lease offered at the increased rent.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to landlords raising rent on residential tenancies.

rules.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot raise the 
rent mid-lease term.

rules.title: No rent increase to cover condominium or cooperative conversion costs
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to a condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Increases to cover new services or amenities are still allowed.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to all tenants in a building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple unit ownership, regardless of senior or disabled protected-tenancy status.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of units.

rules.quoted_span:
If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee 
simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the 
conversion

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict or fail to renew a lease, written or oral, without good cause, and must prove the grounds in court. Every cause except nonpayment of rent must be described in a written notice, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except nonpayment.
rules.key_value: Good cause required for eviction or nonrenewal

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to most residential rentals, including single-family homes, mobile homes and mobile home park land, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes. Excludes owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units, and hotel, motel and guest house transient or seasonal guests.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt where the premises are owner-occupied with two or fewer rental units.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Hotel and motel occupants with no alternate residence who reside there continually are covered. Units held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies them are exempt.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-unit premises with two or fewer rental units; hotel, motel or guest house transient or seasonal guests; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Statute: enumerated grounds for eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant only on one of the statutory grounds listed in the Anti-Eviction Statute, such as nonpayment, disorderly conduct, property damage, lease violations, habitual late payment, a permanent change of use, or conversion. Most grounds require a prior written Notice to Cease and/or a Notice to Quit of 3 days to 3 years before suit is filed.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit ranges from 3 days to 3 years depending on cause

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental tenancies, including mobile home parks, covered by the Anti-Eviction Statute. Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are governed by a separate section.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are handled under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Public housing authorities must also follow HUD regulations.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are subject to a different list of causes (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2).
rules.interaction: Public housing evictions must also follow federal HUD regulations (24 C.F.R. 966). Rent-increase evictions must comply with municipal rent control ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: Listed below are the statutory grounds for eviction as set forth in the Anti-Eviction Statute.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for health/safety and illegal-occupancy evictions
rules.requirement: A tenant evicted for health and safety violations or removal from the rental market cannot be evicted until relocation assistance is provided. A tenant evicted for illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation payment of six times monthly rent, paid by the landlord. The tenant may be paid from a municipal fund if the landlord has not paid at least five days before removal.
rules.key_value: 6 times monthly rent (illegal occupancy); 18% annual interest on unpaid balance

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenants evicted under the Anti-Eviction Statute ground for health and safety violations, illegal occupancy, or governmental removal of property from the rental market.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: The six-times-rent payment applies to evictions for illegal occupancy (G 3); other G causes require eligible tenants to receive relocation assistance before eviction.

rules.interaction: Where a municipality has a revolving relocation fund, the tenant may be paid from it and the landlord must repay the municipality. Where there is no fund, unpaid amounts accrue 18% annual interest and are a lien on the property.
rules.quoted_span: an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

rules.title: Eviction to permanently retire property from residential use
rules.requirement: A landlord who wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use must serve a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing suit. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.

coverage_conditions.summary: Buildings or mobile home parks being permanently retired from residential use, where the health and safety/removal grounds in section G do not apply.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies only where circumstances under section (G) do not apply.

rules.quoted_span: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential

rules.title: Eviction on conversion to condominium, cooperative or fee simple
rules.requirement: A landlord converting a building or mobile home park to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership must serve a Notice to Quit at least three years before filing suit, comply with conversion regulations, and respect court-ordered stays. Protected senior and disabled tenants cannot be sued for possession while their protected tenancy lasts.
rules.key_value: 3 years' Notice to Quit; up to five one-year stays

coverage_conditions.summary: Buildings or mobile home parks being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of two or more units or park sites.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Subject to the exceptions in subsection L for tenancies beginning after the master deed was recorded and for owner occupancy.

rules.exemptions: Subsection L allows eviction on shorter notice (two months) for tenancies that began after the master deed or plan was recorded, and for owner-occupancy or sale-to-occupant cases in buildings with three or fewer units.
rules.interaction: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act and Tenant Protection Act of 1992 provide additional protection.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord must comply with the regulations

rules.title: Evictions in owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only by court order, on specified causes the landlord must prove. A three-month notice to quit applies to at-will and year-to-year tenancies and one month to month-to-month tenancies. A three-day written notice applies to disorderly, destructive or rule-violating tenants.
rules.key_value: Notice to quit: 3 months (at will/year-to-year), 1 month (month-to-month), 3 days (disorderly/destructive/violations)

coverage_conditions.summary: Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings.

rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when

rules.title: Penalties for owner-occupancy and retirement evictions
rules.requirement: A landlord who evicts to personally occupy a unit must occupy it for at least six months, or be liable for treble damages plus fees and costs. A landlord who evicts to board up, demolish or retire a property from residential use must not use it residentially for five years, or be liable for treble damages, fees and costs and a civil penalty.
rules.key_value: 6 months owner occupancy; 5-year bar on residential use; treble damages; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation

coverage_conditions.summary: Landlords who obtain possession by notice of personal occupancy or of boarding up, demolition or permanent retirement from residential use.

rules.quoted_span: the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years.

rules.title: Reprisal protections for tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not take reprisal action by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or refusal to renew when a tenant exercises certain civil rights, such as enforcing lease or legal rights, making good faith health or safety complaints, or organizing or joining a tenant organization.

coverage_conditions.summary: All rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excluded.

rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of

rules.title: Foreclosure is not grounds for eviction; 90-day notice to quit
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. Before evicting a tenant after foreclosure, a buyer who wants to personally occupy the property as a primary residence must give a 90-day notice to quit, and cannot act on a longer lease until it expires.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenants in foreclosed properties; month-to-month tenants and owner-occupied two- and three-family units are not exempt from the 90-day notice.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies where the foreclosed property is bought by a buyer who wants to occupy it as a primary residence.

rules.interaction: Federal foreclosure tenant protections do not preempt State or local laws providing longer periods or additional protections.
rules.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy
rules.requirement: Eligible senior citizen, disabled and certain disabled-veteran tenants in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their income is within the statutory limit.
rules.key_value: 40 years protection; income up to the greater of 3 times county average per-person income or $50,000

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenants aged 62 or older, permanently disabled, or honorably discharged veterans disabled at 60% or more, who lived in the converted building at least one year before the conversion recording date.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Income limit: not more than three times the county average per-person income or $50,000, whichever is greater. Applications are generally due within 60 days. Hudson County tenants may have additional protection under the Tenant Protection Act of 1992.

rules.interaction: Hudson County tenants may be eligible for additional protected tenancy under the Tenant Protection Act of 1992.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years
